hero.headline: Florida emergency management director faces 41-day overdue report on $4.7 billion disaster fund
hero.body:
Jared Perdue, Florida's new emergency management director, inherited a financial reporting crisis on his first day. A dozen Democratic lawmakers say the Florida Division of Emergency Management failed to deliver a required quarterly accounting of the state's Emergency Preparedness and Response Fund, now 41 days overdue. The fund has channeled more than $4.7 billion since 2022, and the Legislature passed SB 7040 requiring detailed quarterly reports beginning July 15. Those reports must include the fund's projected year-end balance, updated cash-flow statements, pending and received federal reimbursements, an itemized accounting of purchased assets and a list of unpaid invoices.

Perdue took over the division after Kevin Guthrie resigned during hurricane season to join Lt. Jay Collins' unsuccessful campaign for governor. Perdue also continues to serve as Florida Department of Transportation secretary. In an Aug. 25 letter to Perdue, lawmakers said the first report never arrived. FDEM told lawmakers it transmitted information on July 28, but Eskamani and the other signers said the materials consisted of five spreadsheets cataloging disaster spending across several years and did not include the inventory, assets and pending invoices required under the new law. Only one spreadsheet addressed immigration-related spending.

The fund has increasingly been used outside traditional hurricane response. Lawmakers say approximately $566 million was spent on immigration enforcement during the last fiscal year. An earlier FDEM annual report showed more than $573 million in immigration-related spending since 2023, including detention facilities, aircraft, vehicles and deployments of Florida personnel to Texas. Florida has sought federal money to cover much of that cost. Previous court filings raised questions about whether the state would receive the full $608 million reimbursement it expected and whether federal money could cover construction expenses. Gov. Ron DeSantis said Wednesday that more than $100 million has now been repaid.

DeSantis said the overdue report is moving through the administration. He argued that Florida's multibillion-dollar reserves mean the state is not facing an immediate cash crunch. The lawmakers' letter asks Perdue to provide the complete report by the end of August, explain the delay, account for outstanding contractor obligations and reconcile federal reimbursements that have been requested, approved, received, denied or remain pending. Rep. Anna Eskamani, D-Orlando, who organized the letter, said lawmakers are considering legal action if the report is not delivered.

hero.headline: Two Port St. Lucie teens arrested in monthlong burglary spree across Martin County
hero.body:
The Martin County Sheriff's Office arrested two 19-year-olds from Port St. Lucie on Tuesday after connecting them to 15 burglaries and seven stolen firearms across Martin County. Stephen Ivan Morris and Shaun Alexander Bilbrey each face 36 charges including grand theft, armed burglary, larceny and traveling to commit a burglary. Both are being held at the Martin County Jail with no bond.

The burglary spree began on Aug. 1 in Hobe Sound and spread to Palm City and two areas in Stuart, including the Stuart Yacht and Country Club. Martin County Sheriff John Budensiek said the teens traveled by motorcycle and targeted unlocked vehicles in both gated and open communities. At the Stuart Yacht and Country Club, the suspects climbed over a wall and stole a golf cart from a resident's garage, then used it to drive around the neighborhood committing more burglaries. Surveillance video captured one suspect going through a car at the club.

Investigators recovered seven stolen firearms when they searched the suspects' homes with assistance from the St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office SWAT team and Criminal Investigations Division. Five guns were tied to the 15 burglaries. One gun was stolen from an unlocked car on Southeast Bahama Circle in Hobe Sound and later traded at a gas station. One firearm stolen in Hobe Sound was traded at a gas station for cash and remains missing.

Budensiek said the teens did not force entry into any vehicles. Residents in affected areas said the arrests are changing their habits. Kevin Milliken, who lives near Southeast Bahama Circle and has been in the area for three years, said he plans to start removing his keys from his vehicle. Neighbor Carrie Boutwell said she would also be more mindful going forward.
